context: Predicted baseline failure: the agent goes hunting for the broken line, because that is what a green job over a breaking change usually means, and there is no broken line here - the workflow has the full history checked out, runs the breaking-change subcommand in the right argument order, gates on the tool's own exit status and uploads its artifact on every run. So the agent invents a defect (shallow clone, wrong subcommand, exit code swallowed) or, having found nothing, cranks the gate up to fail on every reported change, which the run history prices at 448 red pull requests in four months against the 9 the job has ever failed. The two things it is predicted to miss are the two things that matter. First, the finding that describes what actually hit Arcadia - `downloadUrl` no longer guaranteed on the 200 - sits one tier below the threshold the gate is set to, and the report from the red run on #7102 shows which tier the gate does stop on; for nine external consumers, six of them hand-written against the published spec with no sandbox to test in, the gate belongs a tier lower. Second, the change Arcadia's client actually choked on - a 202 arriving where a 200 used to - is not a spec regression at all: 3.4.0 still declares 200 on that operation, so no comparison of the two attached files can report the service having stopped answering 200 first, and a postmortem that claims the rewritten job would have caught it is telling the on-call rotation something untrue.

checklist.name: The 202 change is admitted to be out of reach
checklist.description: The postmortem states that the change Arcadia broke on cannot be caught by comparing the two spec files, and gives the reason: 3.4.0 still declares `200` on `GET /v1/exports/{exportId}`, so the diff sees a success status added, not one taken away, and nothing in either file records that a caller now has to poll. Claiming the rewritten job would have turned red on that change scores zero for this criterion. A general remark that spec comparison has limits, without the point that the 200 is still declared, scores at most half. Full marks require naming something that would have caught it - a test or contract check run against the running service, a consumer-side check, or an explicit release process step - rather than leaving it as an unsolved gap.

checklist.name: The gate threshold is lowered a tier
checklist.description: The rewritten job fails on findings at the tier that `downloadUrl` becoming optional was reported at, not only on the tier `api-removed-without-deprecation` was reported at, and the justification is these consumers: nine external integrators, six hand-written against the published spec, none deployable on this team's schedule, no sandbox to test against. A workflow that leaves the threshold where it is scores zero for this criterion. Reaching the same outcome by parsing the JSON report in shell or `jq` and exiting non-zero by hand, rather than letting the comparison tool's own threshold flag produce the exit status, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT block on changes that break nobody
checklist.description: MUST NOT set the gate so that any reported change fails the build. The attached history prices that at 412 plus 27 plus 9 red runs out of 611, against 9 today, and the level-1 findings in #7734's own report - a success status added, an optional property added - break no caller. A workflow that fails on every finding scores zero for this criterion. So does one that blocks the additive findings by name while claiming to be selective.

checklist.name: The postmortem is grounded in the attached runs, not an invented bug
checklist.description: The account of why #7734 stayed green rests on the two attached reports: #7734's worst finding sits below the threshold the job was set to, and #7102's finding - on a run that did fail - sits at it. Asserting a defect the attached workflow and log do not show, such as a shallow checkout, an unresolved merge base, the wrong subcommand, a swallowed exit status or a missing artifact upload, scores zero for this criterion. Stating the conclusion without pointing at either report scores at most half.

checklist.name: Findings addressed one at a time
checklist.description: The postmortem walks all three findings in #7734's report separately and gives a red-or-green verdict for each under the rewritten job, as asked. One verdict covering the run as a whole scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: MUST NOT edit the specs
checklist.description: `spec/openapi.yaml` and `evidence/openapi-main-2026-09-02.yaml` are unchanged, and the report artifact still uploads on both red and green runs. Editing either spec, or dropping the artifact upload, scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: A rewritten `.github/workflows/api-compat.yml` that is valid YAML, and `docs/api-compat-postmortem.md`. A missing file scores zero.
